links.outcome: Change in medical students' critical thinking with supervised AI-assisted diagnosis use over 12 months
links.effect: Higher AI-assisted diagnosis participation was associated with increases in AI literacy and critical thinking. AI literacy statistically mediated the participation-to-critical thinking association. No erosion of critical thinking was reported under supervision.
links.quote: Higher participation was associated with increases in AI literacy and critical thinking, and AI literacy statistically mediated the participation-to-critical thinking association.

unlisted_practices: Supervised (faculty-guided) use of AI diagnostic tools in medical education to build critical thinking
Building AI literacy as a mediator of benefit from AI use in training

screen.reason: Evaluates the longitudinal impact of medical students' participation in AI-assisted diagnosis during supervised clinical rotations on AI literacy and critical thinking.
